sshleifer.body:
Audited every intermediate consumer to back the policy with evidence rather than assertion:

- The tensor has exactly one consumer before host conversion: `batch_result_processor.py` does `tuple(logits_output.input_token_logprobs.tolist())` — dtype-agnostic. Everything downstream (logprob_result_processor's tuple assert, schedule_batch's `List[Tuple]` holder, multi_tokenizer splitting, disaggregation, OpenAI serving) operates on python floats after that point.
- No `torch.cat`/`copy_`/`.to()`/dt

Also pinned by test now (not just documented): test_fast_path_emits_fp32_logprobs asserts the fast path emits fp32 while the log_softmax path keeps the logits dtype — runs on CPU CI, so the policy can't drift silently.

The NPU platform overwrites the parsed backend in [`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py:80-86`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py#L80-L86):

```python
# handles hierarchical cache configs
if args.enable_hierarchical_cache:
    args.hicache_io_backend = "kernel_ascend"
    if args.use_mla_bac

`kernel_ascend` is not introduced by this PR. It is the existing HiCache NPU
backend identifier used by the NPU platform and the MHA/MLA paths, so this PR
follows the existing naming for consistency.

Renaming it only here would break the dispatch. Would it be okay to keep
`kernel_ascend` for consistency in this PR?
